title: DC Studios: Skydance names ex-Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham president and CCO from 1 Dec; James Gunn and Peter Safran step away after four years
headline: Marvel Veteran Replaces James Gunn at DC From 1 Dec
caption:
Skydance, the company that now owns Warner Bros. and DC, has named former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham president and chief creative officer of DC Studios. He takes over on 1 December from James Gunn and Peter Safran, who ran the studio as co-chairmen and co-CEOs for four years.

Latcham was at Marvel from 2004 to 2017, from Iron Man to The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy and Spider-Man: Homecoming. At DC he will run films, series and animation.

Skydance says Gunn and Safran will return to full-time creative work. Gunn's Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow, is in post-production and still dated 9 July 2027 in the US, with the pair as producers. Superman (2025) grossed $618 million worldwide.

Which DC film would you book a first-day ticket for?

Sources: Skydance, Variety, TheWrap, Deadline

alt_text: Slide 1: a licensed AP photo of James Gunn and Peter Safran, under the headline "Marvel Veteran Replaces James Gunn at DC From 1 Dec". Slide 2: "13 YEARS", Jeremy Latcham's run at Marvel Studios: he helped launch Marvel's film universe with Iron Man; executive producer, The Avengers and Guardians of the Galaxy; he'll lead DC's films, series and animation from here. Slide 3: "9 JUL 2027", Man of Tomorrow's US release date holds: Gunn wrote and directs it, and it is in post-production; Gunn and Safran stay on as its producers; Superman (2025) made $618M worldwide, the bar to beat.
